body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), the explicit local-polynomial learners satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\). In particular, \(\mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n)\) and therefore \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=O_P\{n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\}=o_P(1)\) because \(\beta>5/12\); bounded foldwise empirical increments give \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\); and the smooth plug-in estimates give \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\) and \(|\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)-1|=o_P(1)\). More generally, whenever \(\mathsf G_n\) holds and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), optimized-value stability gives \(\{S_n-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))=o_P(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).
body.justification: This separates the actual product, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds required at the moving Gumbel level from the stronger instrumental assumptions used to verify them.
body.gap: Published pointwise causal-isotonic LR theory requires a nuisance product small relative to one cube-root neighborhood; the displayed conditions add the logarithmic accuracy needed after scanning order \(n^{1/3}\) dependent neighborhoods.
body.consumer: The lemma lets later work replace the local-polynomial implementation by any learner collection that verifies the same four quantitative remainders.

obligation.what_is_open: The centered local empirical bound and the optimized-value stability conclusion have not been derived from the four frozen remainder quantities.
obligation.obstruction: The pseudo-outcomes contain a within-validation-fold empirical marginalization term, so the local process requires a conditional Hoeffding decomposition rather than an independent-sum inequality. Even after that bound, objective perturbation needs common finite-window localization and slope envelopes for both constrained and unconstrained PAVA fits; \(\mathsf G_n\) does not state those properties.
obligation.attempted: The product-bias exponent, variance plug-in rate, and volume plug-in rate were derived. A sup-norm optimized-objective comparison was examined, but without common localization its integration-by-parts boundary and total-variation terms are uncontrolled on the required moving windows.
obligation.partial_result:
If the learner bounds in \(\texttt{lem:learner-rates}\) are available, then the product part of the threshold follows algebraically:
\[
 \mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n),
 \qquad
 n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n
 =O_P\!\left(n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\right)=o_P(1),
\]
because
\[
 \frac56-2\beta=-\frac16+\frac{d+1}{2s}<0.
\]
On the event on which the density estimates stay inside fixed positive bounds, product, quotient, and integration inequalities also give
\[
 \mathfrak K_n=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}),
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathcal V}_n}{\mathcal V(P)}-1\right|
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}+n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
Thus the product, variance, and spatial-clock parts of \(\mathsf G_n\) have the advertised orders.  The unresolved steps are the fold-conditional Hoeffding decomposition needed for \(\mathfrak R_n\), followed by common localization and slope envelopes for both optimized isotonic objectives; the four numerical remainders alone do not supply those geometric properties.
